# Commercial Yeast vs Sourdough

The choice between commercial yeast and a sourdough starter is a choice about
time and flavour more than about leavening power. Both raise a dough by
producing carbon dioxide inside the gluten network; they differ in what else
they do along the way.^[raw/articles/the-science-of-a-good-loaf.md]

## Where they differ

- Commercial yeast raises a dough in a few predictable hours and contributes
  little flavour of its own.
- A sourdough starter takes far longer, and the bacteria living beside the
  yeast produce the acids that read as sourness.
- Those acids also stiffen gluten and slow the flour's enzymes, which is why
  sourdough schedules run longer and gentler than yeast ones.
